test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 11 Aug, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: At an interest rate of 7.7% per annum, the simple interest on a certain sum of money for 2(6)/(7) years is ₹1,188. At an interest rate of 8.5% per annum, how much will be paid in total in 4(5)/(9) years for that sum of money?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective % for Case 1 = 7.7 × 20/7 = 22%

22% of Principal = ₹1,188 ⇒ Principal = ₹5,400

Effective % for Case 2 = 8.5 × 41/9 = 348.5/9%

New Interest = (348.5/9)% of 5400 = 348.5 × 6 = ₹2,091

Total Amount = Principal + New Interest = 5400 + 2091 = ₹7,491

**∴ The correct answer is ₹7,491.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

SI₁ = ₹1,188

R₁ = 7.7% and T₁ = 20/7 years

R₂ = 8.5% and T₂ = 41/9 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Amount = Principal (P) + SI

 
 Principal (P) = ?

 
• 
 
• 

 
 R = 7.7%, T = 20/7 yrs
 SI = 1188
 Find P = 5400

 
 R = 8.5%, T = 41/9 yrs
 Find SI = 2091
 Amount = 7491

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI₁ = (P × R₁ × T₁) ÷ 100

⇒ 1188 = [P × 7.7 × (20/7)] ÷ 100

⇒ 1188 = (P × 1.1 × 20) ÷ 100

⇒ 1188 = P × (22 ÷ 100)

⇒ P = (1188 × 100) ÷ 22 = ₹5,400

Now, finding the interest for the second case:

⇒ SI₂ = (P × R₂ × T₂) ÷ 100

⇒ SI₂ = [5400 × 8.5 × (41/9)] ÷ 100

⇒ SI₂ = 54 × 8.5 × (41/9)

⇒ SI₂ = 6 × 8.5 × 41

⇒ SI₂ = 51 × 41 = ₹2,091

Total Amount = Principal + SI₂

⇒ Amount = 5400 + 2091 = ₹7,491

**∴ The correct answer is ₹7,491.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Interest Rate

The total simple interest over a time period T is directly proportional to the product of Rate and Time. Effective Interest % = R × T.

Amount in Simple Interest

The final accumulated sum is the original Principal plus the generated Interest. Formula: A = P + (P × R × T) ÷ 100.

Principal Invariance

Unlike compound interest, the principal in simple interest remains constant throughout the entire term, making the interest linearly dependent on time.
